title: Most Populous Countries in the World (UN data, mid-year estimates)
caption:
46% of everyone on Earth lives in just five countries.

India and China alone hold 35% of humanity: 2,880 million people.
The US is third, with 24% of India's population.
By the end of the century, the UN projects Pakistan will overtake the US, while China shrinks to 633 million.

Did you guess all five? Which one surprised you?

Source: UN DESA Population Division (World Population Prospects 2024).

title: How Big Is a Trillion? Million vs Billion vs Trillion, Explained
caption:
Counting to a trillion, one number per second, would take 31,688 years.

A million: 11.6 days. A billion: 31.7 years.
In $100 bills, a trillion dollars is 10,000,000,000 notes, weighing about 10,000 tonnes.

Did you know the gap was this big?

caption:
The biggest desert on Earth isn't the Sahara. It's Antarctica.

A desert is defined by how little precipitation falls, not by heat or sand. One common rule: under 250 mm a year.
Antarctica's polar plateau gets about 50 mm. Its desert covers 13.96 million km², the Arctic about 13.7 million.
The Sahara, at 8.6 million km², is still the largest hot desert.

title: Average Height by Country: Tallest and Shortest Men and Women (NCD-RisC)
caption:
Young Dutch women are taller than young men in Timor-Leste, by 10.3 cm.

The Netherlands has the tallest 19-year-olds: 183.8 cm for men, 170.4 cm for women.
The shortest: men in Timor-Leste (160.1 cm) and women in Guatemala (150.9 cm).
That is a 23.7 cm gap for men and 19.5 cm for women.
The researchers point to diet and health during childhood as key factors.

Do you feel tall or short where you live?

title: Which Countries Have No Rivers? Saudi Arabia and Six More
caption:
Saudi Arabia covers 2,149,690 km² and has no permanent river.

UN FAO water surveys describe the same in the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Djibouti and Malta: valleys that flood briefly after storms, then run dry.
Renewable fresh water per person: Kuwait about 6 m³ a year, Saudi Arabia 66, the world average 6,702.
Lists online vary. Yemen, Libya and Oman often appear too; we kept only the clearest cases.

title: Human History in 24 Hours: When Farming, Writing and the Web Appear
caption:
Squeeze 300,000 years of Homo sapiens into one day and the Web has existed for about 10 seconds.

Each hour of the day is 12,500 years.
Farming starts about 58 minutes before midnight.
Writing: about 25 minutes before midnight.
The Industrial Revolution: the last 77 seconds.

Which invention changed the most in those last seconds?

title: How Many Undersea Internet Cables Are There? Length, Count and Traffic Share
caption:
The internet isn't in the sky. It's on the seabed.

607 submarine cable systems are in service, with 102 more planned (TeleGeography, Sep 2026).
Together they stretch over 1,500,000 km, enough to circle the Equator more than 37 times.
The ITU says they carry more than 99% of international data traffic. Satellites carry just 0.37% of US international capacity.

Did you think the internet went by satellite: yes or no?

title: Which Countries Work the Most Hours? Annual Hours Worked per Worker (OECD 2025)
caption:
The average worker in Mexico puts in 873 more hours a year than one in Germany.

Mexico tops the OECD with 2,205 hours per worker in 2025, then Costa Rica (2,183) and Chile (1,912).
Germany works least: 1,332 hours, followed by Denmark (1,369) and Norway (1,386).
The OECD average is 1,736; the United States is at 1,800.
Part-time work pulls averages down, so these are not full-time hours.

Which country would you rather work in?

Source: OECD (Average annual hours actually worked per worker (OECD Employment database)); OECD, reported by The Korea Times (S. Korea's yearly working hours fall by 32 hours last year but remain longer than OECD average); OECD, via Apiar Data (Colombia average annual hours worked (OECD AVERAGE_HOURS_WORKED)).

title: How Much Would Sea Level Rise If Antarctica Melted? (Bedmap3 Data)
caption:
If all of Antarctica's ice melted, global sea level would rise about 58 metres.

The ice sheet holds 27.17 million km³ of ice, on average 1,948 m thick (Bedmap3 survey).
At its thickest it reaches 4,757 m, and under the grounded ice 47% of the bedrock lies below sea level.
It holds roughly 61% of all the fresh water on Earth.

Did you know Antarctica's ice was this thick?

Source: British Antarctic Survey et al., Scientific Data (Bedmap3 updated ice bed, surface and thickness gridded datasets for Antarctica (Pritchard et al., 2025)); GRID-Arendal (UNEP collaborating centre) (Icebergs, Antarctic Peninsula).
